title: Fisheries Statistics
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned 200L Fisheries Statistics curriculum: descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, range, variance, standard deviation), sampling techniques, probability basics, correlation and regression, catch-per-unit-effort (CPUE), and applied calculation problems using typical fisheries data (catch, length, survival rate).

questions.question: Fisheries statistics is primarily concerned with:
options: The collection, analysis, and interpretation of numerical data related to fish populations and fisheries activities
The classification of fish species by external morphology
The construction of fishing gear
The study of fish diseases
questions.correct_answer: The collection, analysis, and interpretation of numerical data related to fish populations and fisheries activities
questions.explanation: Fisheries statistics applies statistical methods to fisheries and aquaculture data, such as catch records, growth measurements, and survey results, to support scientific analysis and management decisions.

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of a data set is calculated as:
options: The sum of all values divided by the number of values
The middle value when data are arranged in order
The most frequently occurring value
The difference between the highest and lowest values
questions.correct_answer: The sum of all values divided by the number of values
questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean (average) is obtained by summing all observations and dividing by the total number of observations in the data set.

questions.question: Given the fish weights (in grams): 120, 150, 130, 140, 160, what is the mean weight?
The median of a data set is defined as:
options: The middle value when the data are arranged in ascending or descending order
The sum of all values divided by their count
The value that occurs most frequently
The largest value in the data set
questions.correct_answer: The middle value when the data are arranged in ascending or descending order
questions.explanation: The median splits an ordered data set into two equal halves; for an odd number of observations it is the single middle value, and for an even number it is the average of the two middle values.

questions.question: Given the fish lengths (in cm): 22, 25, 21, 28, 24, what is the median length?
questions.explanation: Arranged in order: 21, 22, 24, 25, 28. With five values, the median is the middle (3rd) value, which is 24.

questions.question: The mode of a data set refers to:
options: The value that occurs most frequently in the data set
The average of all values
The middle value in an ordered data set
The range of the data
questions.correct_answer: The value that occurs most frequently in the data set
questions.explanation: The mode is the most commonly occurring value(s) in a data set, and a data set can have one mode, more than one mode, or no mode at all.

questions.question: Given the catch data (number of fish per net haul): 5, 7, 7, 8, 9, 7, 10, what is the mode?
questions.explanation: The value 7 appears three times, more than any other value in the data set, making it the mode.

questions.question: The 'range' of a data set is calculated as:
options: The difference between the highest and lowest values
The sum of all values
The average of all values
The middle value of the data set
questions.correct_answer: The difference between the highest and lowest values
questions.explanation: Range is a simple measure of dispersion calculated by subtracting the minimum value from the maximum value in a data set.

questions.question: Given fish weights (in grams): 90, 110, 105, 130, 95, what is the range?
questions.explanation: Range = maximum - minimum = 130 - 90 = 40 grams.

questions.question: Variance in statistics measures:
options: The average of the squared deviations of each value from the mean
The most frequent value in the data set
The middle value in an ordered data set
The total sum of all data values
questions.correct_answer: The average of the squared deviations of each value from the mean
questions.explanation: Variance quantifies how spread out data values are around the mean by averaging the squared differences between each observation and the mean.

questions.question: Standard deviation is best described as:
options: The square root of the variance, expressed in the same units as the original data
The same as the mean
The square of the variance
A measure of central tendency, not dispersion
questions.correct_answer: The square root of the variance, expressed in the same units as the original data
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is derived by taking the square root of the variance, making it more interpretable since it shares the same units as the original measurements.

questions.question: A small standard deviation in a sample of fish lengths indicates that:
options: The individual lengths are clustered closely around the mean
The lengths are widely and evenly spread out
All the fish are of different species
The sample size is definitely too small to be valid
questions.correct_answer: The individual lengths are clustered closely around the mean
questions.explanation: A low standard deviation reflects low variability, meaning most observed values lie close to the mean, whereas a high standard deviation indicates greater spread.

questions.question: In fisheries sampling, 'random sampling' is a technique in which:
options: Every individual (or sampling unit) in the population has an equal chance of being selected
Only the largest fish are deliberately selected
Samples are chosen based on convenience only, regardless of representativeness
Only fish from a single specific location are ever selected
questions.correct_answer: Every individual (or sampling unit) in the population has an equal chance of being selected
questions.explanation: Random sampling ensures each unit in the population has an equal probability of selection, minimizing selection bias and improving the representativeness of the sample.

questions.question: Stratified sampling in fisheries surveys involves:
options: Dividing the population into distinct subgroups (strata) and sampling from each subgroup
Selecting only one sample from the entire population regardless of subgroup
Sampling exclusively from the largest subgroup available
Avoiding any form of subdivision of the population
questions.correct_answer: Dividing the population into distinct subgroups (strata) and sampling from each subgroup
questions.explanation: Stratified sampling divides a heterogeneous population into more homogeneous strata (e.g. by depth zone or gear type) and samples each separately, improving precision of overall estimates.

questions.question: A key advantage of random sampling over convenience/haphazard sampling in a fish stock survey is that random sampling:
options: Reduces bias and allows valid statistical inference about the whole population
Is always cheaper to conduct regardless of circumstances
Guarantees a sample with no variability at all
Eliminates the need for any data analysis
questions.correct_answer: Reduces bias and allows valid statistical inference about the whole population
questions.explanation: Because random sampling gives every unit an equal chance of selection, it minimizes systematic bias and provides a statistically valid basis for generalizing results to the broader population.

questions.question: Catch per unit effort (CPUE) is calculated as:
options: Total catch divided by the amount of fishing effort expended
Total fishing effort divided by total catch
The number of fishers involved multiplied by catch
The market price divided by catch weight
questions.correct_answer: Total catch divided by the amount of fishing effort expended
questions.explanation: CPUE = catch / effort (e.g. kg of fish per net-hour or per boat-day), and is commonly used as an index of relative fish stock abundance.

questions.question: A fisher catches 60 kg of fish after fishing for 5 hours with one gillnet. What is the catch per unit effort (CPUE) in kg per hour?
options: 12 kg/hour
300 kg/hour
5 kg/hour
60 kg/hour
questions.correct_answer: 12 kg/hour
questions.explanation: CPUE = total catch / effort = 60 kg / 5 hours = 12 kg per hour.

questions.question: If a fleet of 10 boats fishes for 4 days each and lands a total of 4,000 kg of fish, what is the CPUE in kg per boat-day?
options: 100 kg/boat-day
400 kg/boat-day
40 kg/boat-day
1,000 kg/boat-day
questions.correct_answer: 100 kg/boat-day
questions.explanation: Total effort = 10 boats x 4 days = 40 boat-days. CPUE = 4,000 kg / 40 boat-days = 100 kg per boat-day.

questions.question: A declining CPUE trend over several years, assuming fishing methods remain constant, is generally interpreted as an indicator of:
options: A possible decline in fish stock abundance
An increase in fish stock abundance
Improved water quality
No relationship to stock abundance whatsoever
questions.correct_answer: A possible decline in fish stock abundance
questions.explanation: Since CPUE is often used as a proxy for stock abundance, a sustained decline (with constant gear/effort standardization) suggests the underlying fish population may be shrinking, possibly due to overfishing.

questions.question: Correlation analysis in fisheries statistics is used to determine:
options: The strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables
The exact cause-and-effect relationship between two variables
The total sample size needed for a survey
The mode of a single data set
questions.correct_answer: The strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables
questions.explanation: Correlation quantifies how strongly two variables (e.g. fish length and weight) are linearly associated and whether that association is positive or negative, without implying causation.

questions.question: A correlation coefficient (r) close to +1 between fish length and weight indicates:
options: A strong positive linear relationship, where weight tends to increase as length increases
No relationship at all between the two variables
A strong negative relationship between the two variables
That length and weight are measured in identical units
questions.correct_answer: A strong positive linear relationship, where weight tends to increase as length increases
questions.explanation: A correlation coefficient near +1 signifies that as one variable increases, the other tends to increase proportionally as well, indicating a strong positive linear association.

questions.question: A correlation coefficient (r) of 0 between two variables suggests:
options: No linear relationship exists between the two variables
A perfect positive linear relationship
A perfect negative linear relationship
The two variables are identical
questions.correct_answer: No linear relationship exists between the two variables
questions.explanation: An r value of 0 indicates the absence of any linear association between the variables, though a non-linear relationship could still exist.

questions.question: In regression analysis, the 'dependent variable' is:
options: The variable whose value is predicted or explained by the independent variable(s)
The variable used to predict outcomes but not itself predicted
A variable with no relationship to the analysis
Always measured in kilograms
questions.correct_answer: The variable whose value is predicted or explained by the independent variable(s)
questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome being modeled or predicted (e.g. fish weight), while the independent variable (e.g. fish length) is used to explain or predict it.

questions.question: A survival rate calculation in a hatchery trial: 800 fry were stocked and 640 survived to fingerling stage. What is the percentage survival rate?
questions.explanation: Survival rate = (number surviving / number stocked) x 100 = (640/800) x 100 = 80%.

questions.question: A fish farmer stocks 1,200 fingerlings and harvests 900 fish after six months. What is the percentage mortality?
questions.explanation: Number of deaths = 1,200 - 900 = 300. Mortality rate = (300/1,200) x 100 = 25%.

questions.question: A pond stocked with 5,000 fingerlings yields a total harvest weight of 2,500 kg after eight months. What is the average weight per fish at harvest?
options: 0.5 kg
5 kg
2 kg
0.2 kg
questions.correct_answer: 0.5 kg
questions.explanation: Average weight = total harvest weight / number of fish = 2,500 kg / 5,000 = 0.5 kg per fish.

questions.question: In a sample of 50 fish, 30 are female and 20 are male. What percentage of the sample is female?
questions.explanation: Percentage female = (30/50) x 100 = 60%.

questions.question: A researcher records the following fish counts caught in five successive net hauls: 12, 15, 18, 10, 20. What is the mean catch per haul?
A hypothesis test in fisheries research is used to:
options: Statistically evaluate whether an observed pattern in the data is likely due to chance or reflects a real effect
Always prove a theory is absolutely true with complete certainty
Replace the need for any data collection
Determine only the mean of a data set
questions.correct_answer: Statistically evaluate whether an observed pattern in the data is likely due to chance or reflects a real effect
questions.explanation: Hypothesis testing uses probability-based statistical methods to assess whether observed differences or relationships in sample data are likely to reflect a genuine effect in the population, rather than random variation.

questions.question: In probability, an event with a probability of 0 means:
options: The event will never occur
The event will always occur
The event has a 50% chance of occurring
The probability cannot be determined
questions.correct_answer: The event will never occur
questions.explanation: A probability of 0 indicates impossibility, while a probability of 1 indicates certainty; probabilities range from 0 to 1.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'sample' as opposed to a 'population' in fisheries statistics?
options: A subset of individuals selected from the entire population for study
The complete set of all individuals of interest
A term used only for laboratory-reared fish
A synonym for the word 'species'
questions.correct_answer: A subset of individuals selected from the entire population for study
questions.explanation: A sample is a manageable subset drawn from the larger population, used to make inferences about that population without needing to study every individual.

questions.question: A frequency distribution table in fisheries data analysis is used to:
options: Organize data by showing how often each value or range of values occurs
Calculate the exact market price of fish
Replace the need for graphical presentation entirely
Determine the geographic origin of the fish sample
questions.correct_answer: Organize data by showing how often each value or range of values occurs
questions.explanation: A frequency distribution summarizes raw data by tallying how many times each value (or class interval) occurs, making patterns in the data easier to see and analyze.
